title: FactoryContinuation
description: The link a Factory outcome (`factory.outcome.json`'s `source`) carries back to the terminal legacy record it continues, WITHOUT rewriting that record's own history (spec-factory.md §3: 'a continuation is a new Factory ID with a unique source link, never an in-place edit of an app-studio record'). This schema describes the link only — it never re-specifies `app.mission`'s own shape or lifecycle, and `app.mission.json` gains nothing from this release. Modeled from the repo's own proven PlantPal migration path (`factory.service.migrate_plantpal`), which is the only continuation Factory has actually built to date (spec-factory.md open question 5 — 'the migration example, not a completed delivery pilot').

system.description: The owning hexagon of the legacy record — always `app-studio` today (the only system Factory reads legacy missions from, spec-factory.md §4). A `const` rather than an open enum: a second legacy source is a new capability, not a value this field should silently start accepting.

id.description: The legacy `app.mission` id this outcome continues. Read-only reference — Factory never writes to this id.

receipts.description: Opaque per-artifact provenance receipts captured at continuation time (one entry per legacy artifact read, e.g. `plan.json`, `registration.json`, keyed by artifact name; `mission` for the mission record itself). Left as an open map rather than re-specified here: the receipt shape is app-studio's own artifact-read provenance, not a Factory- or contracts-owned type, and duplicating it here would risk drifting from whatever app-studio's own read API actually returns.

approvedWaves.description: Legacy wave identifiers already approved before this continuation was created — carried forward so Factory's own criteria never re-litigate already-approved scope.

outstandingWaves.description: Legacy wave identifiers not yet delivered as of the continuation — the scope this outcome's `criteria` were derived from.

claimBoundary.description: The legacy record's own claim-boundary text at continuation time, preserved verbatim so a later reader can see exactly what the legacy record claimed and did not claim.

legacyStage.description: The legacy record's own lifecycle stage at the moment this continuation was created — must be a terminal stage (spec-factory.md §3: 'only terminal legacy missions may create a continuation'). Free text over app-studio's own stage enum, not duplicated here, so a new legacy stage name is never a breaking change to this schema.
